title: Local Integral Transforms and Global Spectral Decomposition
summary: An exact permitted Q3 complementary-series example produces an uncancelled double pole on an allowed Theorem2(1) contour. Theorem2(2) omits its diagonal exclusion. Selected normalization, changes of variables, global residue algebra and application manipulations checked correctly; no general failure of the spectral strategy asserted.

problems.title: Theorem 2(1)'s advertised forward contour strip and holomorphy assertion
problems.source_location: Theorem 2(1), equation (1.12), physical p. 5; initial assumptions and γ convention, p. 3; proof §2.7, p. 17.
problems.claim: For all θ1<σ<1/2−θ, the forward χ-integral is absolutely convergent and its χ-integrand is holomorphic in θ1<Re(χ)<1/2−θ.
hypotheses: F=Q3 and ψ has conductor Z3. The self-dual additive measure has vol(Z3)=1; d×y=dy/|y|.
π1=π=I(1) are irreducible generic tempered unramified principal series of PGL2(Q3). Set θ1=θ=0.
π2=I(|.|^(−1/4)) is an irreducible unitarizable generic complementary principal series, with θ2=1/4. The source permits I(χ2) for some character and imposes no Re(χ2)≥0 condition in its setup.
Take χ2=|.|^(−1/4), χ0=1, W1(a(u))=1_(1+3Z3)(u), and W2(a(u))=1_(2+3Z3)(u). These functions are real, so the conjugations visible in the source do not alter this test.

The proposed vectors may be constructed directly from (2.9)-(2.10): on the open Bruhat cell take f_j(wn(x))=(1/3)ψ(a_j x)1_(3^(−1)Z3)(x), with a_1=1,a_2=2, and inducing characters 1 and |.|^(−1/4), respectively. A compactly supported smooth section on that cell extends by zero to the induced model. Fourier inversion gives the stated unit-coset restrictions, since the factors |u|^(1/2)χ_j(u)^(−1) equal 1 on their supports.

The hypotheses of Theorem 1 also hold for this example because θ1+θ2+θ=1/4<1/2. With target π tempered and χ0 unitary, the D=1 decay assertion in Lemma 2.6 gives absolute convergence of the defining h-sharp integral.
complete_check: For y∈2+3Z3, multiplication sends z∈1+3Z3 into yz∈2+3Z3. Otherwise the two supports cannot meet. Consequently H(y,1)=(1/3)1_(2+3Z3)(y).

On 2+3Z3, both |y| and |1−y| are 1. Therefore, for the unramified character χ=|.|^s, the inner y-integral in (1.12) is exactly (1/3)vol(2+3Z3)=1/9 for every s. This rules out cancellation by the test function.
For I(1), L(u,I(1))=(1−3^(−u))^(−2). The unramified ε-factor for the chosen ψ is 1. Definition (1.6) therefore gives γ(u,I(1))=[(1−3^(−u))/(1−3^(u−1))]^2.
At s=1/4, the second denominator has a zero of order two. Every other factor is finite and nonzero. Explicitly lim_(s→1/4)(s−1/4)^2 G(s)=(1/9)[(1−3^(−3/4))/(1−3^(−1/4))]^2(1−1/3)^2/(log 3)^2>0.

Thus the integrand has a genuine uncancelled double pole inside the advertised strip 0<Re(s)<1/2. On the allowed contour Re(s)=1/4, the local absolute value behaves as a positive constant times |Im(s)|^(−2). The unramified component of the character Haar measure has nonzero continuous measure there, so this contour integral is not absolutely convergent.

This is a verified restriction for the example and consistent with the source's derivation; it is not a new certification of every case of a repaired theorem. problems.title: Theorem 2(2) omits the diagonal exclusion or an explicit extension convention
problems.source_location: Theorem 2(2), physical p. 5, compared with Theorem 1(2), p. 4 and proof §2.7, p. 17.
problems.claim: The formula is quantified for y∈F×, including y=1.
hypotheses: y=1 is allowed by the printed quantifier
complete_check: At y=1, χ(1−y) and χ0(1−y) are evaluations of multiplicative characters at zero, outside their domain, and |1−y| is zero. The displayed right side therefore has no literal value at that point.
The proof substitutes (y1,y2)=(z,yz) in Theorem 1(2), whose hypothesis y1≠y2 requires y≠1, then changes z by multiplication with (1−y)^(−1). It supplies only the off-diagonal formula.
The full extracted manuscript was read; no separate diagonal extension convention was found in the stated local formulas or their proof.
The left side at y=1 need not vanish. For example, take χ0=1 and equal nonzero real compact Kirillov restrictions w; then H(1,1)=integral |w(z)|^2 d×z>0.

There is a natural local repair: state y≠1, or explicitly define the right side at y=1 by the smooth extension from H(y,χ0). Because the fixed z-support is compact and away from zero, H is smooth in y (locally constant in the nonarchimedean case), so this extension exists whenever the proved off-diagonal equality applies.

problems.counterevidence: The off-diagonal formula's factors match the change of variables. H itself supplies a smooth diagonal extension.
problems.repair: State y≠1 or explicitly define the diagonal value by smooth extension from H.
problems.repair_verification: Compact z support away from0 permits differentiation/local constancy under the H integral; this gives the extension where the off-diagonal identity holds.

problems.severity_reason: Local domain omission with an explicit extension or exclusion; no failure of off-diagonal inversion shown.

result: Write u=zt and v=(t−1)/t in the forward transform followed by the shift Mellin transform. For fixed t, d×z=d×u and χ0(z)=χ0(u)χ0(t)^(−1).
Off v=0,1, t=(1−v)^(−1) and d×t=|v|/|1−v| d×v. Also |t/(t−1)|^(1/2)=|v|^(−1/2), while χ(t)^(−1)χ0(t)^(−1)=χ(1−v)χ0(1−v). The resulting weight is exactly conjugate(χ2)(v) sqrt(|v|)/|1−v| as printed.

For inversion, set y1=z and y2=yz with y≠1. Theorem 1's prefactor becomes conjugate(χ2)^(−1)(y) sqrt(|y|)/|1−y|. In the shift Mellin integral substitute u=z(1−y); multiplicative Haar invariance gives the additional χ0(1−y)^(−1). This matches Theorem 2(2)'s printed prefactor off the diagonal.

The final Fourier/Mellin multiplier in §2.6 has the character orientation required by (2.4), with the reciprocal functional-equation factor turning into γ(1,π1⊗conjugate(χ2)⊗χ^(−1)). The source's compactly supported convolution expression provides cancellation and analytic continuation for the entire inverse multiplier; that does not prove cancellation of the forward multiplier with π fixed.
These changes of variables preserve the contour initially supplied by Theorem 1. They alone do not justify removing θ2 from the lower contour bound.

checks.source_claim: Theorem 2(1), source PDF page 5, equation (1.12): absolute convergence and holomorphy throughout theta1 < Re chi < 1/2-theta. Setup on pages 3-4,9-13 and the derivation on page 17 were checked.
checks.independent_reasoning: For Q3 with conductor-Z3 psi, self-dual additive volume(Z3)=1 and multiplicative measure dy/|y|, take pi1=pi=I(1), pi2=I(|.|^-1/4), theta1=theta=0 and theta2=1/4. Normalized I(chi) has parameters chi and chi^-1; these examples are irreducible generic unitary, the last in the complementary range. Page 3 permits some inducing character and page 11 defines theta by absolute real parameters, imposing no nonnegative sign on Re chi2. Compact sections f_j(wn(x))=(1/3)psi(a_j x)1_(3^-1 Z3)(x), a1=1,a2=2, in (2.9) give exactly W_j(a(z))=1_(a_j+3Z3)(z), since the character and norm factors are one on units. Then H(y,1)=(1/3)1_(2+3Z3)(y). Both y and 1-y are units there, so the inner integral is 1/9 for every unramified chi=|.|^s. From (1.6), gamma(u,I(1))=[(1-3^-u)/(1-3^(u-1))]^2. The full integrand is (1/9)[(1-3^(-1/2-s))/(1-3^(-1/2+s))]^2[(1-3^(-5/4+s))/(1-3^(1/4-s))]^2. At s=1/4 only the last denominator vanishes, to order two. Its leading coefficient is positive and nonzero. The permitted contour Re s=1/4 therefore has nonintegrable |Im s|^-2 behavior on its positive-Haar-measure unramified component. This directly disproves both advertised analytic assertions. Lemma 2.6 with theta=0 and eta<1/2 also makes the chi0=1 defining h-sharp integral absolutely convergent.
checks.counterevidence_and_impact: Theorem 1's theta1+theta2<sigma<1/2-theta contour excludes the pole and its nonempty-strip condition holds in this example. The substitutions on page 17 preserve that original contour and do not remove the pole of a fixed-pi forward integrand. The entire inverse multiplier discussed earlier on page 17 is a different expression and supplies no cancellation here. Choosing the other inducing character would change the stated data; no sign restriction or continuation prescription is part of the assertion tested. The false domain belongs to a main local transform theorem and supports Major under the original calibration, while failure of all transforms, tempered cases or global results is not claimed. The report accurately limits the proposed repair rather than proving an optimal replacement theorem.

checks.source_claim: Theorem 2(2) on page 5 quantifies y in F-times, compared with the off-diagonal hypothesis in Theorem 1(2) on page 4 and proof on page 17.
checks.independent_reasoning: The allowed value y=1 makes chi(1-y) and chi0(1-y) evaluations outside the domain of a multiplicative character and makes the displayed |1-y| denominator zero. In the actual proof, y1=z and y2=yz violate y1!=y2 at y=1, and multiplication by (1-y)^-1 is unavailable. The left side is nevertheless defined, and with equal nonzero real compact restrictions and chi0=1 it is the positive integral of |w|^2. No literal value for the displayed right side is supplied by the source.
checks.counterevidence_and_impact: For compact restrictions away from zero, H(y,chi0) is smooth, or locally constant in the nonarchimedean case, near y=1 by differentiation or local constancy under its fixed compact z-integral. Excluding y=1 or explicitly taking the extension supplied by H repairs this local domain omission where the off-diagonal identity is valid. This does not fix P001's separate strip problem. Minor is appropriate.
